summary: Hiroshi Araki specializes in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He earned his degrees, including a PhD in 2013, at Kyoto University. He taught at Aichi Prefectural University and Osaka University, and served as Professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (2010–2025).

Hiroshi Arami is a scholar in Sinology and Buddhist studies. In 2026, he is attested as a lecturer at both the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.
Hiroshi Deguchi studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1948 to 1953. He later held a post at Hokkaido University from circa 1957 to 1963.
Hiroshi Kanaseki was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1948 to 1951 and held a post at Tenri University from circa 1951 to 1998.

Hiroshi Kanno works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Tokyo and held posts at Toho Kenkyukai, Soka University, and the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology, where he served as Director (circa 2003–2009).

Hiroshi Kuroda is an Indology and philosophy scholar who completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University in 1976. He was an assistant professor at Osaka Gakuin University, attested between 1983 and 1988.

Hiroshi Marui is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo (BA, PhD 2011) and under Albrecht Wezler. His posts included the Eastern Institute, Musashino University, and an assistant professorship at the University of Tokyo (1999–2018).
Hiroshi Maruyama was a scholar active in Indology and other fields. Attested in 1987, he served as a professor at Osaka University and headed the Ayurveda Kenkyukai.
Hiroshi Nemoto works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned an MA at Hiroshima University, where he served as an associate professor (attested 2015) and professor (attested 2026).
Hiroshi Tokushige is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Koyasan University as a commissioned researcher (attested 2015) and as a specially appointed lecturer (attested 2026).
Hiroshi Yamashita is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Madras. He served as an associate professor at Tohoku University, attested from 1996 to 1999.

Hirotaka Kato is a Buddhist studies scholar. He was a research assistant at the Chion'in Research Institute of Jodo Buddhism (attested 2015) and an associate professor at Kyoto Bunkyo University (attested 2026).

Hirotomo Teranishi served as a professor and assistant vice-president at Soka University in 2010. He succeeded Hiroshi Kanno in 2009 as Director of the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology, holding the role into the 2010s.
Hisanosuke Izui was a linguist who studied at Kyoto University from circa 1927 to 1930. He later held an academic post at Kyoto Sangyo University from circa 1968 to 1981.

Hisao Inagaki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University and earned a PhD at the University of London. He taught at SOAS (1969–1981) and served as Professor at Ryukoku University (1981–1998).

Hisao Kanaseki studied at Doshisha University and worked in Buddhist studies and other fields. He served as a professor at Kobe University (circa 1952–1968), Tokyo Metropolitan University (circa 1968–1982), and Komazawa University (circa 1982–1989).

Hisao Takahashi is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied under Ryukai Mano at Taisho University, where he also spent his career as an assistant, lecturer, and professor (circa 2002–2015).

Hisashi Matsumura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. His academic posts include the Australian National University (attested 1982) and an assistant professorship at Kobe Shinwa University (attested 1996).

Hisashi Sato was a Tibetology and history scholar who studied at Kyoto University (circa 1934–1937). He served as a professor at Kyoto University (circa 1963–1977), Bukkyo University (circa 1977–1987), Toyo University, and Komazawa University.

Hisataka Ishida works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned a Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna in 2011 under Helmut Krasser, having also studied under Akira Saitō. He served as a lecturer at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 2015).
